title: Blind benchmark and injection-recovery test of f26_ebfit.py, registered before any fit was run

method.code: f26_ebfit.py as of commit 098af75 (the model, priors, detrending and trust rule are not changed for this test)
method.allowed_changes: faster sampling only: a process pool and running the chain in blocks until it is at least 20 autocorrelation times long after burn-in (cap 6000 steps). Neither changes the model or the likelihood.
method.inputs_per_system: TESS SPOC 2-minute light curves of every available sector; the published period and time of primary eclipse (our candidates get these from the pipeline); the eclipse duration and the secondary-eclipse phase are measured from the folded light curve by f29_benchmark.py, not taken from the paper
method.note_30min: 30-minute runs average the 2-minute data, as for AI Phe, to mimic full-frame-image light curves

pass_rule.source: the AI Phe tolerances already in f26_ebfit.py, unchanged
pass_rule.esinw_note: compared as |e sin omega| because papers using JKTEBOP and ellc can differ in the sign convention for omega; e and e cos omega are compared with sign
pass_rule.a_system_passes: all six checks pass at that cadence
pass_rule.reporting: every system and cadence is published as it comes out, including failures; no system may be dropped or swapped after the fits

systems.name: MU Cas
systems.reference: arXiv:2410.23011 (MU Cas, JKTEBOP fits to TESS), Table II, mean of sectors
systems.why: B-type pair, P = 9.7 d, e = 0.19: the period and eccentricity range of the candidates

systems.name: V1022 Cas
systems.reference: Southworth, Rediscussion of eclipsing binaries Paper III (arXiv:2012.05978), Table II
systems.why: partial eclipses at i = 83 deg, e = 0.31: the hardest geometry for separating the two radii

systems.name: V454 Aur
systems.reference: Southworth, Rediscussion of eclipsing binaries Paper XIX (arXiv:2404.19443), Table II
systems.why: long period, small stars, e = 0.38; few eclipses per sector

systems.name: V505 Per
systems.reference: Southworth (arXiv:2106.04323), Table II; circular orbit assumed there
systems.why: circular control: the method must not invent an eccentricity

injection_recovery.purpose: measure bias and whether the quoted 68% intervals contain the truth about 68% of the time, on the candidates' own noise and sampling
injection_recovery.hosts: candidate light curves (data divided by their best-fit model gives real noise, gaps and cadence); hosts chosen to span cadence: one 30-minute, one 10/30-minute, one 2/3-minute
injection_recovery.grid: 16 synthetic systems per run drawn with a fixed seed: rsum 0.08-0.30, k 0.6-1.0, i giving both eclipses, e 0-0.4, omega uniform, J 0.4-1.0, l3 0-0.15; period and ephemeris of the host
metrics: median bias of e, e cos w, r1, r2, i
fraction of injections whose 68% interval contains the truth
for injections the trust rule accepts: fraction with |e error| <= 0.03
for injections it rejects: the same fraction
injection_recovery.trust_rule_recalibration: if accepted injections have |e error| <= 0.03 in fewer than 80% of cases, or rejected ones in more than 80%, the rsum threshold is moved to the value that best separates them and the change is reported; the candidate verdicts are then recomputed with the new threshold
